title: GTA6 Changes the Run Button After 25 Years
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is changing how sprinting works. According to reports, the game no longer requires players to tap a face button to run.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## A Quarter-Century Tradition Comes to an End in GTA6

For nearly 25 years, the Grand Theft Auto series has maintained a very specific and distinct control mapping for movement. In almost every major installment, getting your character to sprint required players to repeatedly tap a face button on their controller. Depending on the platform, this meant rhythmically mashing either the X button or the A button just to move at high speed.

While some titles developed by Rockstar Games offered alternative control schemes over the years, the default setting has consistently required this button-tapping mechanic. However, according to recent reports from gaming outlet Eurogamer, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally bucking this long-standing trend.

## Analyzing the Shift in Modern Game Controls

This mechanic has been a staple of the franchise since the series made its landmark transition into 3D environments, becoming an ingrained part of the muscle memory for millions of players worldwide. Although traditional button mashing became a familiar quirk of the series, modern action game design has increasingly favored more ergonomic and seamless movement controls.

While specific details regarding the exact new default control scheme for GTA 6 were not fully outlined in the source material, moving away from repetitive face-button tapping represents a significant quality-of-life update. Navigating open worlds and engaging in high-stakes action sequences will likely feel vastly different under a modernized control layout.

## Editor's Take

Dropping a 25-year-old control convention is a bold yet welcome move for Rockstar Games. While veteran fans might initially need a moment to adjust their muscle memory, modernizing the sprint input reduces unnecessary controller strain and aligns the franchise with contemporary gaming standards for smoother traversal.
